_comment: The channel line-up this demo publishes, kept deliberately identical in name, source clip and
stream directory to rt-mbms-examples' and rt-dvb-i-examples' own channels.json, so the three
demos show the same content under the same names.
Per channel:
id       stable identifier, used in log lines and in the external service id
name     what the service is called wherever a name is shown
source   file under $HOME/MWC_TV_RADIO that the looping live encoder plays
stream   directory the encoder writes under the media origin's public/ directory
type     linear or radio, the DVB-I demo's own vocabulary. A radio channel is encoded
audio-only: see live-encoder.sh for why that matters over a broadcast bearer
onAir    true if this channel is carried over the radio as its own MBS User Service. The
others are still encoded and served by the origin, so every demo offers the same
four channels; they are simply not broadcast here.
ssmDest  destination of this channel's own source-specific multicast group. Required when
onAir, and must be unique: two Distribution Sessions cannot share an SSM, and the
MBSF rejects the second with the SSM already in use.
Only one channel is on air. Two MBS Distribution Sessions can be created and both reach the
UE -- packets for each group arrive on tun_bcastue at a similar rate -- but only the second
session's objects complete: with two sessions sharing the bearer, the first session's larger
objects lose enough blocks that they are never recovered, and a broadcast bearer has no
retransmission. The same channel on its own delivers its segments without trouble. This is a
limitation of the RAN this demo runs over, not of the line-up, and it is recorded in the
project's srsRAN_Project_mbs findings register as the MBS scheduling-contention defect.
Set onAir true on a second channel to reproduce it; ssmDest is already assigned for that. The
rt-mbms-examples demo, on a different radio stack, does carry both of its on-air services.
